title: A Summer in the Cage

synopsis: "A Summer in the Cage" is filmmaker Ben Selkow's feature-length documentary chronicling his friend Sam's battle with manic-depressive illness, also known as bipolar disorder. The film follows Sam for seven years as he suffers delusional manic episodes, battles paralyzing depressions, and tries to escape the legacy of his bipolar father who committed suicide when Sam was eight years old. By showing the difficult emotional impact of being bipolar on Sam, his family, all those who care about him and the filmmaker, "A Summer in the Cage" hopes to put a human face on an illness that affects millions of American families. But as this dramatic story unfolds and heads to an explosive standoff, it also becomes a unique tale about friendship and the ethical responsibilities of a documentary filmmaker.

Life as she knew it is now over. With the help of her father, Ian, Maura works to reclaim her life and waits for a miracle to bring her daughters home. To make this film is to make your voice heard, it is to try to order the chaos of its tragic existence, it is to free speech and end the silence in order to continue living.

Both sides have different things to deal with, the manic Andrew has lots of energy and ideas, he doesn't require much sleep and in order to deal with his overage of energy he runs, the depressive Andrew is suffering from insomnia, is uncreative, non productive and in battle with his inner self.

title: Bipolarized: Rethinking Mental Illness
evidence: Ross McKenzie’s own experience with bipolar disorder is at the centre of the documentary.
synopsis: BIPOLARIZED is about one man's personal journey to heal. Diagnosed with bipolar disorder, Ross' psychiatrist told him he would live with the disorder for the rest of his life and that he would have to take lithium to control symptoms. To Ross, taking the drug daily felt like a chemical lobotomy, leaving him in a foggy, drug-induced haze. Ross ultimately decided to resolve his symptoms outside of conventional medicine. He progressively reduced his use of the psychotropic drug lithium, at an experimental clinic in Costa Rica. What ensued was a self-exploration into alternative treatments to treat his condition and a journey delving into the root cause of his mental breakdown. The film uses Ross' personal experiences to tell a larger story about medication. It will reveal how we are labelling more and more people with mental illnesses and how, in tandem, we are prescribing more and more toxic psychotropic drugs to treat these illnesses.

In showing how one family deals with generations of loss and grief, the film defies the stigma related to mental illness and suicide and tells a human story that touches everyone.

As Trevor contends with his own brain, he’ll discover a nearly twenty-year-old secret that may determine whether he conquers his illness, or if his illness conquers him.

Their honest interaction reveals that Josh has a good friend, Chase, with the same condition. And that the right medication can transform emotionally crippling mood swings and delusional thoughts into a satisfying and productive future. Marlow is ready to learn more and his life is instantly saved.—David Rabadi

title: Can

While taking an anti-depressant, he experienced a manic episode. In his mania, he bought a brand new car for $32K, and he had grandiose ideas about changing the world. He thought he could single-handedly leverage the stock market. Can was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and was eventually forced to leave college. Over a 12-year period, Can tried more than 20 different medication and underwent 15 electro-convulsive shock treatments.

The actress-writer recounts stories about her work on the "Star Wars" series as well as her relationship with her parents Eddie Fisher and Debbie Reynolds. The title refers to Chris' belief that his late father, who loathed Richard Nixon, is now friends in heaven with the former president. Ranging over three generations of Murrays, whose patriarchs struggled with alcoholism and bipolar disorder, the film treats of subjects ranging from father-son relationships to the Great Depression, from the effects of divorce on families to the cushy lifestyle of the residents of Southhampton, New York.

Having failed to find a publisher for his written account, he invited the filmmaker into his house to record his battle to ‘tame the tiger’ through willpower.

title: Deadly Jails

This investigative short looks at how advocacy organizations like the Mental Health Association of Oklahoma are trying to change the way these counties handle urgent mental health situations.

synopsis: Damon Smith has estimated that he has spent around 50,000 hours of his life, so far, participating in absurd ritualistic behaviours associated with his obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD).  With a diagnosis of both, OCD and Bipolar Disorder, and with the help of his anxious friend, Adam Coad, these Australian singer-songwriters share, through original music, preposterous humour, and outlandish animations, the intricate and debilitating nature of what it is like to live and talk about mental illness in a world where it’s ok to talk about a broken arm, but not ok to talk about a broken mind.

title: Mi cabeza me hace trampas
evidence: Carlos Mañas’s bipolar diagnosis is the focus of this documentary.

title: Michael Clayton
evidence: Arthur Edens is described as having bipolar disorder in the film, which also shows him stopping his medication.
synopsis: A law firm brings in its "fixer" to remedy the situation after a lawyer has a breakdown while representing a chemical company that he knows is guilty in a multi-billion dollar class action suit.

title: Midsommar
evidence: Dani mentions that her sister Terri is bipolar while discussing a worrying message from her.
synopsis: Several friends travel to Sweden to study as anthropologists a summer festival that is held every ninety years in the remote hometown of one of them. What begins as a dream vacation in a place where the sun never sets, gradually turns into a dark nightmare as the mysterious inhabitants invite them to participate in their disturbing festive activities.

title: Mina två liv
evidence: Ann Heberlein meets other people affected by bipolar disorder in this documentary series.

title: Mind/Game: The Unquiet Journey of Chamique Holdsclaw
evidence: Chamique Holdsclaw’s bipolar disorder forms part of this account of her mental health and recovery.
synopsis: Women's college basketball player Chamique Holdsclaw battles mental illness.

title: Modern Love
evidence: Lexi lives with bipolar disorder in the Modern Love episode based on Terri Cheney’s essay.
directors: John Carney; Tom Hall; Sharon Horgan; Logan George; Emmy Rossum; Jesse Peretz; John Crowley; Andrew Rannells; Marta Cunningham; Celine Held

title: Mon ami Batman Tremblay
evidence: Raphaël “Batman Tremblay” has recently received a bipolar diagnosis in this short documentary.

title: Montagnes Russes
evidence: Bipolarity is the central theme of this film about Antoine, without implying that the director has the condition.
synopsis: A tender love story about a bipolar man navigating his mental health while trying to grow emotionally and professionally.

title: Mood Atlas
evidence: Shane lives with bipolar disorder and works with a neuroscience team to map his brain.
synopsis: Shane spent the last ten years taking mood stabilizers, antidepressants, antipsychotic drugs, anti-anxiety pills, sleeping pills, and so on. Along the way he lost his job, his girlfriend and his friends. Mood Atlas is a short documentary exploring Shane’s Bipolar Disorder and his search for hope in neuroscience. As a team of brain researchers map his brain, the psychological tests administered to Shane act as a device for the film viewer to enter Shane’s psyche.

title: Moon Unit
evidence: Moonie grows up with a mother who lives with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: An East-German teenager is growing up with her bipolar mother during the 2000s. When the opportunity arises to spend a year abroad, the already turbulent universe of mother and daughter threatens to collapse.

title: Mr. Jones
evidence: Mr. Jones is diagnosed with bipolar disorder, though he questions whether his doctors have enough evidence.
synopsis: The story about the relationship between a manic depressive man, Mr. Jones, and the female doctor who takes more than a professional interest in his treatment.

title: My Brother Khosrow
evidence: Khosrow lives with bipolar disorder, which shapes his stay in his brother’s home.
synopsis: Khosrow (Shahab Hosseini) who is a bi-polar man is forced to live in his brother's house Nasser, as his guardian and sister goes abroad for a while. The brothers soon find themsleves in friction due to the challenging behavior of Khosrow and quesrionable moral decisions by Nasser.

title: My Brother's Keeper
evidence: Jare receives a bipolar diagnosis and begins taking medication for his mood.
synopsis: The story of a Finnish rap artist Cheek and his brother.

title: My Salinger Year
evidence: Daniel is described as bipolar in a brief conversation after his death.
synopsis: A college grad takes a clerical job working for the literary agent of the renowned, reclusive writer J.D. Salinger.

title: Nerkonda Paarvai
evidence: Lawyer Bharath Subramaniam is described as living with bipolar disorder and acute mania.
synopsis: When three young women are harassed and implicated in a crime they didn't commit, a bipolar lawyer sets out to help them clear their names and prove it to everyone that a woman's consent matters.

title: Neurotransmitting
evidence: Theo and Ruth Cuthand discuss hospitalisation connected to bipolar disorder.
synopsis: TJ Cuthand and his mother Ruth Cuthand have a candid conversation about TJ’s last hospitalization for Bipolar Disorder in 2007. While TJ only knew his manic episode from the inside, Ruth had to deal with caregiving decisions and trying to find help. While they reminisce they also have to reckon with the feelings of animosity that arose between them during these events.

title: Next to Normal
evidence: Diana Goodman lives with bipolar disorder in this filmed musical.
synopsis: Diana Goodman, a suburban mom, comes to terms with her bipolar disorder and the effect her struggle has on her family. It is a gripping and honest portrayal of how one suburban family grapples with mental illness touching on issues such as grieving, suicide, drug abuse and ethics in modern psychiatry. This contemporary musical deals tenderly with how far two parents will go to keep their family’s world intact.

title: Next to Normal
evidence: Diana Goodman’s bipolar disorder is central to this filmed West End production.
synopsis: A mother struggles with worsening bipolar disorder and the effects that managing her illness has on her family. The PBS Great Performances recording of the West End transfer to Wyndham's Theatre (from The Donmar Warehouse) in 2024.

title: No estoy loca
evidence: Silvia, another patient at the psychiatric clinic, is described as bipolar.
synopsis: A woman enters a quirky mental health clinic after attempting suicide upon finding out her husband is having an affair with her best friend.

title: No Letting Go
evidence: Timothy's family struggles to come to terms with his bipolar diagnosis.
synopsis: A young teenager struggles with a debilitating mental illness as his mom risks everything to save him without losing the rest of her family.

title: Normal Litio
evidence: Massimiliano Marianni draws on his own experience of bipolar disorder in this film.
synopsis: In a room (a mental prison): the only way out is to enter oneself.  Normal Lithium is inspired by bipolar disorder, the loss of self and hope, and the inner search for salvation.  Symbols accumulate in a journey to find balance, even as those same symbols wildly invade the image.

title: Numbness
evidence: Mary, Jalal’s sister, lives with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Jalal, a dropouts philosophy student, realizes that her sister Mary, who has a Bipolar disease, is married to a bourgeois man named Shahrokh who is addicted to football betting. He left the house angrily, and goes to his friend's house, Bahman, who is an underground composer. He meets a strange taxi driver named Nasser on his way. They spent a strange night together.

title: Observe and Report
evidence: Ronnie Barnhardt says he has bipolar disorder and has stopped taking his medication.
synopsis: Mall security guard Ronnie Barnhardt is called into action to stop a flasher from turning shopper's paradise into his personal peep show. But when Barnhardt can't bring the culprit to justice, a surly police detective is recruited to close the case.

title: OC87: The Obsessive Compulsive, Major Depression, Bipolar, Asperger's Movie
evidence: Actor Maurice Benard, one of the people Bud Clayman meets, lives with bipolar disorder.
directors: Bud Clayman; Glenn Holsten; Scott Johnston
synopsis: Director Bud Clayman documents his struggle with OCD and Asperger's Syndrome and how it derailed his plan to become a filmmaker.

title: Of Two Minds
evidence: People living with bipolar disorder share their experiences in this documentary.
synopsis: Of Two Minds explores the extraordinary lives, struggles and successes of three unique and compelling people living with bipolar disorder in America today. Through a combination of intimate verité and revealing interviews, we experience what it feels like to be bipolar - from exquisite feelings of grandiosity and sensuality to the depths of despair and depression. A journey from the painful to the painfully funny, Of Two Minds puts a human face on the illness, opening an engaging, harrowing and perception-changing view on those all around us who live in bipolar's shadows...our sisters and brothers, parents and friends, and ourselves.

title: On the Inside
evidence: Mia lives with bipolar disorder and forms a bond with another patient.
synopsis: A decent but troubled young man is sent to a psychiatric institution for the criminally insane and soon finds himself in a fight for his life battling ghosts inside his head and very real enemies all around him.

title: One Eyed Girl
evidence: A clinician briefly refers to Rachel’s mother as bipolar while reviewing Rachel’s history.
synopsis: After the death of his girlfriend, Travis, a thirty-something psychiatrist, struggles to keep it together. On the brink of a nervous breakdown he stumbles across a strange church run by a charismatic leader, Pastor Jay. In search of answers Travis is led deeper and deeper into the underworld of religious fanaticism, home to a Doomsday cult and a teenage girl named Grace.

title: Orso
evidence: Louison lives with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Louison is bipolar. She often provokes Orso who is madly in love with her. This love story is destined to fail, but he has faith in it. When Louison disappears, everything collapses. He calls Mara, Louison's twin sister. Their relationship is unclear. Which game is she playing ? Orso will have to pursue his ideas to free himself.

title: Pack Up Your Sorrows
evidence: Singer Meg Hutchinson discusses learning to live with bipolar disorder.

title: Parlour Palm
evidence: The short follows a young woman as her mania escalates.
synopsis: An overworked lawyer attempts to care for his partner while she descends into a climate crisis inspired, anxiety fuelled manic episode.

title: Patient Seven
evidence: Patient Three, Gabrielle, is described as living with severe bipolar disorder.
directors: Danny Draven; Paul Davis; Ómar Örn Hauksson; Nicholas Peterson; Rasmus Wassberg; Johannes Persson; Joel Morgan; Erlingur Thoroddsen; Dean Hewison
synopsis: Dr. Marcus, a renowned psychiatrist, has selected 6 severe mentally ill and dangerous patients from the Spring Valley Mental Hospital to interview as part of research for his new book. As Dr. Marcus interviews each patient, one by one the horrors they have committed begin to unfold. However, Dr. Marcus soon learns that there is one patient who ties them all together - Patient Seven.

title: Pelican Blood
evidence: Stevie lives with bipolar disorder and faces stigma from those around her.
synopsis: Nikko is a twenty-something man with good friends, a passion for birdwatching, and self-destructive tendencies. When he falls back into a relationship with Stevie—his seductive, aggressive environmental activist ex-girlfriend he first encountered on a suicide website—his stable existence takes a turn towards chaos once again.

title: Persona: The Dark Truth Behind Personality Tests
evidence: Kyle Behm’s experience with bipolar disorder is part of the film’s examination of personality tests and employment.
synopsis: A documentary exploring the history and growing dangers surrounding the seemingly innocuous Myers–Briggs personality test.

title: Petit Tom
evidence: The documentary follows a family affected by bipolar disorder through the filmmaker’s cousin and her son Tom.
synopsis: Tom is 6 years old. With his camera, he films his mother, the dog, and the alley. Tom has difficulties with studying; he is hyperactive; he has anger issues at school; moreover, he eats crisps for supper. Tom is the son of Nathalie, a loving drug-addicted bipolar mother; the brother of Caroline, an escort who would like to go back to school; and the grandson of Madeleine, the grandmother tired of taking care of everyone. Petit Tom is a film about life and childhood in the setting of chaos, flowing time, family heritage, and motherly love.

title: Pharma Infinity Dance
evidence: Chanika Svetvilas draws on her experience with bipolar disorder in a dance filmed in a pharmacy.
synopsis: Chanika Svetvilas threaded her collection of prescription bottles with galvanized wire to create the shape of a large infinity loop sculpture. Created with an iPhone 8, she dances through the aisles of a CVS pharmacy with her Infinity sculpture to reflect on side effects, the intersections of treatment, access, and stigma as well as their contradictions. As an interdisciplinary artist, Chanika plays with scale to magnify and make visible the relationship between medical conditions, BigPharma, access, side effects and care. Her work developed based on her personal experiences as someone who has a diagnosis of bipolar and as a way to understand and translate meaning through the lens of disability justice and mad pride.

title: Please Like Me
evidence: Josh’s mother Rose lives with bipolar disorder in this series.

title: Point 453
evidence: The film follows a family affected by a boy's untreated bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Point 453 chronicles the growth of an untreated bipolar boy as he struggles to fit into a family that rejects him.

title: Polar
evidence: This animated film draws on people’s accounts of living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: An avalanche changes a polar bear's life, sending him on a journey across a barren fantasy world. A rich narrative exploration of mental health.  Inspired by testimonials on bipolar disorder, this disorienting frame by frame animated short gives life to the experience of millions through fantasy, vivid colour, and metaphor.

title: Poly Styrene: I Am a Cliché
evidence: Poly Styrene’s experience of bipolar disorder is part of this documentary about her life and music.
synopsis: The death of punk icon and X-Ray Spex front-woman Poly Styrene sends her daughter on a journey through her mother's archives in this intimate documentary.

title: Prodigal Sun
evidence: Evelyn’s parents recall protecting her during her first major manic episode in this autobiographical film.
synopsis: Soon after Evelyn realizes she is transgender, her parents sense she is simultaneously experiencing mental illness. As Evelyn struggles for independence, afraid of losing herself to her role in her nuclear family, her parents must fight to keep her safe. Prodigal Sun explores this conflict from both perspectives, as protective parents recount protecting the filmmaker during her first major bipolar manic episode, and Evelyn depicts her reluctance to accept help from those who love her most.

title: Quebonafide: Północ, Południe
evidence: Quebonafide recounts his own experience of bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A hybrid film story, combining the form of a musical with elements of a music film and a personal documentary. The central character and narrator of the story is Quebo – a renowned artist who disappeared from the scene and now returns to speak about his struggle with bipolar disorder.

title: Raising Bipolar
evidence: Families raising children diagnosed with bipolar disorder share their experiences in this documentary.
synopsis: Follow 4 families raising children diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder - a single mother whose son Chase has been hospitalized 6 times; a grandmother raising 4 kids diagnosed with Bipolar Disorder, a little girl, Samantha, who was diagnosed at age 3, and Kelsey, a courageous pre-teen who heroically manages her moods, even as she faces the intensifying social pressures in school.

title: Regarding Gravity
evidence: Bruce, one of the documentary’s two main subjects, lives with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Friends Christian, 63, and Bruce, 71, each have their burden to bear: Christian suffers from a genetic condition that severely impairs his vision and makes his skin hypersensitive to sunlight, while Bruce is hard of hearing and bipolar. But both men share a desire: to defy gravity, to rise up against the limitations of their bodies. As a very composed and rational person, Christian has mastered the techniques of paragliding, and, after years of struggle, he has been given permission to fly on his own. He is now persuading the more erratic and turbulent Bruce to do the same and follow him all the way to Mont Blanc... An intimate and moving portrait of two non-conforming individuals, this "direct cinema" piece with surrealist undertones takes us on a journey into the luminous heights and the dark intricacies of the human psyche.

title: Remake
evidence: Ross McElwee reflects on his son Adrian’s struggles with bipolar disorder and opioid use.

title: Repentance
evidence: Angel Sanchez is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: An earnest life-coach/author, Thomas Carter, is mysteriously abducted by a deranged client, Angel Sanchez, who delves into Thomas' teachings and uses his spiritual messages of Karma - action and reaction (Vipaka), against him to terrorize him and his family for their past sins.

title: Ride the Tiger: A Guide Through the Bipolar Brain
evidence: People diagnosed with bipolar disorder describe their lives in this documentary.
synopsis: Nearly 6 million Americans have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder and yet little is known about how the illness manifests itself in our brains. Ride the Tiger tells the stories of accomplished individuals who have been diagnosed with bipolar, and explores treatment options.

title: Roads of Fear
evidence: Elon is a young man living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Elon, who suffers bipolar disorders, wants to please his dad, head of a southern France mafia, and reluctantly commit crimes. However, each of his acts have consequences, and a heavy price to pay.

title: Rude Dude: The Steve Rude Story
evidence: Comic-book artist Steve Rude’s bipolar disorder affects his work and family life in this documentary.
synopsis: Possessed of an incredible artistic talent, Steve Rude is "The Dude," an eccentric personality as colorful as his comic book art. Filmmaker Ian Fischer (Magritte Moment) presents Rude's rise through the comic book world and difficult transition from comic book shops to art gallery walls, made all the more challenging by Rude's battles with mental illness.

title: Runner
evidence: Vytas had been hospitalised for bipolar disorder before the events of the film.
synopsis: When Marija learns that her unstable boyfriend has disappeared, she takes to the streets in an attempt to find him.

title: Running from Crazy
evidence: Joan “Muffet” Hemingway’s mental illness is discussed using the imprecise label “bipolar schizophrenia.”
synopsis: Running from Crazy' is a documentary examining the personal journey of model and actress Mariel Hemingway, the granddaughter of Ernest Hemingway, as she strives for a greater understanding of her family history of suicide and mental illness.

title: Running with Scissors
evidence: Deirdre Burroughs is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Young Augusten Burroughs absorbs experiences that could make for a shocking memoir: the son of an alcoholic father and an unstable mother, he's handed off to his mother's therapist, Dr. Finch, and spends his adolescent years as a member of Finch's bizarre extended family.

title: Sans cicatrice
evidence: Julie and her son take part in this documentary about her bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Sans cicatrice tells the story of an evolving relationship between a mother and her son. The mother is bipolar and lives through intense episodes. After years, the mother becomes stable and they decide to make a film together, in which they play their proper role. This shared project symbolizes the end of their chaotic journey.

title: Schatten fressen
evidence: Artist Anke Ames discusses her bipolar disorder in this short documentary.

title: Seeing Allred
evidence: Gloria Allred’s former husband Peyton Bray is discussed as having bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Gloria Allred overcame trauma and personal setbacks to become one of the nation’s most famous women’s rights attorneys. Now the feminist firebrand takes on two of the biggest adversaries of her career, Bill Cosby and Donald Trump, as sexual violence allegations grip the nation and keep her in the spotlight.

title: Selena Gomez: My Mind & Me
evidence: Selena Gomez discusses her bipolar diagnosis in this documentary about her mental health.
synopsis: After years in the limelight, Selena Gomez achieves unimaginable stardom. But just as she reaches a new peak, an unexpected turn pulls her into darkness. This uniquely raw and intimate documentary spans her six-year journey into a new light.

title: Separate Lives
evidence: Darlene is briefly called a classic bipolar case during a classroom discussion of mania and depression.
synopsis: Tom Beckwith has just quit his job as a police officer in order to study psychology. But his professor, Lauren Porter, is more interested in his criminology abilities than in his progress in psychology. Because of traumatic circumstances during her childhood she is suffering from multiple personality disorder, and it looks like her other ego may have killed someone. So Tom tries to help her by observing her, combining his professional abilities as an ex-cop and his recently gained knowledge of psychology.

title: September Says
evidence: Sheela, the sisters’ mother, is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Sisters September and July share an intense bond, speaking in a secret language and keeping the outside world at a distance. After September is suspended from school, their mother brings them to a remote house on the Irish coast—where July begins to resist her sister’s increasingly sadistic control.

title: Servants’ Quarters
evidence: Amy Mustafi’s bipolar disorder is part of the workplace crisis at the centre of this film.
synopsis: A lawyer with bipolar disorder moves to her husband's new countryside estate. After finding a sealed door to old servants' quarters, she faces supernatural events that challenge her grip on reality.

title: Shameless
evidence: Ian Gallagher struggles to accept his bipolar diagnosis and the treatment recommended for him.

title: Sick Boys Die Alone
evidence: The short follows a comedian described as having a bipolar diagnosis, though he is not identified as the real friend who inspired the story.
synopsis: After a lifetime of unfortunate events, a diagnosed bipolar and depressed comedian shares his last jokes on an unexpected crowd.

title: Silver Linings Playbook
evidence: Pat Solitano has bipolar disorder and is still coming to terms with his diagnosis after leaving hospital.
synopsis: After losing his job and wife, and spending time in an institution, a former teacher winds up living with his parents. He wants to rebuild his life and reconcile with his wife, but his father would be happy if he shared his obsession with the Philadelphia Eagles. Things get complicated when he meets Tiffany Maxwell who offers to help him reconnect with his wife if he will do something very important for her in exchange.

title: Single Sexy Bilingual
evidence: The film explores being bisexual, bipolar and bilingual.
synopsis: Love is always chaos, especially when you're bisexual, bilingual and bipolar.

title: Sisters Love Forever
evidence: Marin Siem lived with bipolar disorder, a part of her life remembered in this documentary.
synopsis: Wilde and Marin are sisters and best friends. Marin suffers from bipolar disorder and Wilde has been trying to save her for years. Wilde understands that Marin has decided to end her life. This presents Wilde with a major dilemma.

title: Sky, Zyprexa, Night
evidence: Poet Vera Arden struggles with bipolar disorder in this film.
synopsis: A bipolar woman and her two grandchildren are swept into the strange orbit of an evangelical healer’s tent revival tour during the summer of 1993.

title: Slapface
evidence: A schoolgirl briefly tells Lucas that her mother is bipolar.
synopsis: A boy deals with the loss of his mother by creating a relationship with a dangerous monster.

title: Slippers
evidence: Jo’s father is portrayed as having bipolar disorder in a story drawn from the filmmaker’s family experience.
synopsis: Erratic messages from her dad sends Jo deep into the California desert to sort through the remains of a frenzied, paranoid manic episode. However, along the way she makes two discoveries: her family can no longer support him, and the trunk of his car is filled with hundreds of slippers.

title: Something Went Click
evidence: Caryn Cline explores her mother's experience of bipolar disorder.
synopsis: The origin story of my mother's struggle with manic-depression (aka bipolar disorder): the rural prairie in the 1950s, an old boys’ club of “deciders,” a puzzling disease about which little was known. I interviewed my mother in 2000, using a DV camera, but never managed to complete a piece I was satisfied with. After her death, I rephotographed a singular gesture from that video interview onto high-con film (Kodak 3378), then developed cyanotypes from and optically printed (including direct bi-packing with leaves) those sequences onto Kodak 50D.

title: Somewhere Only We Know
evidence: Peng Zeyang’s mother has a history of bipolar disorder and is receiving psychiatric care.
synopsis: Jin Ying is currently experiencing two of life’s most depressing moments: She is jilted by her fiancé, and her loving grandmother passes away. Heartbroken, she decides to visit the European city of Prague, and hopes to use the time to heal her inner pain. While in Prague, she meets a young Chinese man named Punk. There, she slowly unravels a secret romance her grandmother once experienced long ago.

title: Spinning Out
evidence: Figure skater Kat Baker lives with bipolar disorder in this series.

title: Spoken Word
evidence: Poet Cruz Martinez is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A San Francisco spoken word artist returns to New Mexico to be with his dying father, only to find he loses his "voice" as he is sucked back in to the dysfunctional life of drugs and violence he left behind.

title: Spyral
evidence: The documentary looks at the toll of bipolar disorder on a woman and her family.
synopsis: Using a variety of sources, SPYRAL follows one bipolar woman and the impact it has on her family.

title: Steal This Movie
evidence: Abbie Hoffman receives a diagnosis of bipolar I disorder in the film.
synopsis: Five years after Yippie founder Abbie Hoffman goes underground to avoid a drug-related prison sentence, he contacts a reporter to get out the story of the FBI's covert spying, harassment and inciting of violence they then blame on the Left.

title: Stephen Fry: The Secret Life of the Manic Depressive
evidence: Stephen Fry describes his own life with bipolar disorder alongside other people who share their experiences.

title: Storm Alerts
evidence: Marteinn Helgi Sigurðsson re-examines his life after receiving a bipolar diagnosis that the film questions.
synopsis: Is a world obsessed with medical diagnostics and pharmaceutical prescription ready for the vivid testimony of Marteinn Helgi Sigurðsson, who defies the label of ‘bipolar disorder’ to give us a glimpse into his shaman-like wisdom? This inventive docu-drama takes us right inside complex mental experiences.

title: Summer Survivors
evidence: Paulius experiences a manic phase of bipolar disorder in this film.
synopsis: A psychology postgraduate student escorts two patients and their nurse to a seaside psychiatric clinic. Along their journey, they break through each other's barriers, delve into the sources of their various traumas, and discover the lasting imprints left on their fragile souls.

title: Sumotherhood
evidence: Riko says he is bipolar after discussing an episode.
synopsis: Riko and Kane have got it all: big dreams, no respect and a fifteen grand debt. Could things get any worse? Yes! So, it’s time to man up and finally be taken serious as “Roadmen”. Once putting their heads together on various ways to make some money, they decide to rob a megastar in a nightclub toilet and hold up the local bank but things inevitably don’t go to plan!

title: Sunny Intervals and Showers
evidence: Dr. Allan Levi has recently been diagnosed with bipolar disorder in this family documentary.
synopsis: How does bipolar disorder - manic depression - impact on relatives of sufferers? Storyville charts the changes in one such family.

title: Take Me as I Am, Whoever I Am
evidence: Lexi says she has lived with bipolar disorder since she was 15.

title: Taurewarewa
evidence: Three wāhine Māori share their experiences of bipolar disorder in this short documentary.
synopsis: A short documentary on bipolar disorder, Taurewarewa explores the highs and lows of tides and emotions in a sequence of insightful kōrero framed against a backdrop of Aotearoa's turbulent oceans.

title: Taylor Tomlinson: Look at You
evidence: Taylor Tomlinson discusses her bipolar II diagnosis in this stand-up special.
synopsis: Breakups. Therapy. Bangs. Taylor's gone through some stuff since her quarter-life crisis, and she spins her mental health journey into insightful comedy.

title: Technically Crazy
evidence: Jay is a 16-year-old runaway living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A sixteen-year-old, bipolar, runaway named Jay breaks into the house of a retired former cop named Bill, just as Bill reaches rock bottom due to his own issues. These two move from distrust to understanding and come to realize that even though they might drive each other crazy, technically or otherwise, they need each other. Together they help fix what's broken in one another.

title: Thaaram Theertha Koodaram
evidence: Food-delivery worker Sanjay lives with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A food delivery boy, Sanjay, suffers from bipolar disorder and has been abandoned by his family. He tries to take care of two homeless girls in order to prove his ability to socialize.

title: The 108 Journey
evidence: Hugo Rozon’s experience of bipolar disorder is central to this documentary.
synopsis: Hugo, a 24-year-old man, decides to leave his home and travel around the world. His mission? To meet new people and learn new things that might help him find a solution to a condition that’s impacting his life: bipolar disorder.

title: The Ages of Love
evidence: Psychiatrist Eliana Rame says Gaia Arpea has bipolar disorder.
synopsis: In Italy, three men fall in love with three women. First a young engaged lawyer has a fling, then the middle-aged married man has a fling, then a retired man falls in love with his friend's daughter.

title: The Apizaco Shaman
evidence: Bullfighter El Pana’s bipolarity is one of several mental health issues discussed in this documentary portrait.
synopsis: The stormy life of the Mexican bullfighter Rodolfo Rodríguez Gonzalez and his alter ego "THE PANA", of very humble origin, who worked as a baker, gravedigger, bundles loader, seller of gelatinas, before he became a bullfighter. A man to the conquest of his dreams and the glory that slips between his hands because of the bipolarity, the schizophrenia, the narcissism and his eternal addiction to the alcohol.

title: The Book of Solutions
evidence: Filmmaker Marc Becker is portrayed as paranoid and bipolar.
synopsis: Marc, a bipolar and paranoid filmmaker, cannot tolerate seeing his current project picked apart by his producers. The clips he’s been able to sneak a look at lead him to fear the worst. With his editor as an accomplice, he manages to spirit away the rushes to his aunt’s place in the Cévennes, to finish the film as he envisions it. Instead, its completion is constantly postponed, as he creates endless diversions and impasses, which alternate between the comic and the downright disturbing.

title: The Bridge
evidence: Kevin Hines discusses the role of bipolar disorder in the events covered by this documentary.
synopsis: The Bridge is a controversial documentary that shows people jumping to their death from the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco - the world's most popular suicide destination. Interviews with the victims' loved ones describe their lives and mental health.

title: The Butcher Boy
evidence: Francie Brady's mother is portrayed as having bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Francie and Joe live the usual playful, fantasy filled childhoods of normal boys. However, with a violent, alcoholic father and a manic depressive, suicidal mother the pressure on Francie to grow up are immense. When Francie's world turns to madness, he tries to counter it with further insanity, with dire consequences.

title: The Butterfly Room
evidence: Ann is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A reclusive and butterfly-obsessed elderly lady suffering from bipolar disorder develops a disturbing relationship with a mysterious but seemingly innocent youngster.

title: The Dark Horse
evidence: The film portrays chess player Genesis Potini living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: One-time Maori speed-chess champ, Genesis Potini, lives with a bi-polar disorder and must overcome prejudice and violence in the battle to save his struggling chess club, his family and ultimately, himself.

title: The Drummer and the Keeper
evidence: Drummer Gabriel keeps his recent bipolar diagnosis from his bandmates.
synopsis: The Drummer and the Keeper tells the story of the unlikely friendship formed between two young men: Gabriel, a reckless young drummer who revels in rejecting society’s rules and Christopher, a 17-year-old with Asperger’s Syndrome, who yearns to fit in. This heartwarming story shows the strength of the human bond in the face of adversity.

title: The Enormity of Life
evidence: Casey says his mother has both bipolar disorder and paranoid schizophrenia.
synopsis: After a failed suicide attempt, a man receives a substantial inheritance from a long lost relative and meets a struggling single mom with an eccentric young daughter. Together they embark on a journey of self discovery and healing.

title: The Flames of Me
evidence: Daniel Léger recalls his first manic episode and the bipolar diagnosis that followed.
synopsis: How do you rebuild your sense of self after being diagnosed with bipolar disorder? Daniel Léger experienced his first manic episode in his early thirties. With courage and vulnerability, he recounts how his diagnosis shook his identity to the core. Through striking images created with fire and soot by visual artist Steven Spazuk, the film depicts Léger’s personality in rich nuances of shadow and light. The transformations paint a sensitive portrait of a man who, despite his mental health struggles, has been able to rise from the ashes.

title: The Flying Scotsman
evidence: Graeme Obree’s mental health struggles are part of the film, and he later described receiving a diagnosis of bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Based on the incredible true story of amateur cyclist Graeme Obree, who breaks the world one-hour record on a bike he made out of washing machine parts.

title: The Ghost and the Whale
evidence: Joseph Hawthorne is portrayed as a man living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A man, Joseph, loses his wife at sea, then spirals deep into a world of confusion. The wife's brothers' need revenge! Joseph tries to tell anyone who will listen that a whale killed his beautiful Annabel Lee, but even he doesn't quite remember the truth. A journey into the depths of his mind, a conversation with a whale and blood thirsty brothers.

title: The Girl He Met Online
evidence: Gillian Casey is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A man's relationship with a bipolar woman becomes dangerous.

title: The God Committee
evidence: Walter Curtis identifies himself as bipolar during an evaluation.
synopsis: Medicine, money and morality clash when a hospital's Heart Transplant Selection Committee has only minutes to decide which of three patients on the transplant list will receive a heart that has suddenly become available.

title: The Hero's Journey to the Third Pole
evidence: Two people’s experiences of bipolar disorder are the focus of this musical documentary.
synopsis: Part road movie, part musical, part serious inquiry into the caverns of the mind. Þriðji pólinn follows Anna Tara Edwards, an Icelander raised in Nepal, and legendary musician Högni Egilsson, as they journey to Anna’s childhood home in the mountain jungles to explore the afflictions and superpowers that come with bipolar disorder.

title: The Hive
evidence: Alice’s bipolar disorder shapes her relationship with her daughters.
synopsis: As far as they can remember, Marion, Claire and Louise have been living at the pace of their mother Alice’s ups and downs. Now, love is everything that they have left to fight the spiral of self-destruction in which Alice is sinking even more deeply. An unconditional love as violent as it is indescribable.

title: The Holly Kane Experiment
evidence: Holly learns that her mother was bipolar during a discussion of her family’s mental health history.
synopsis: An obsessive psychologist attempts to reprogramme her subconscious mind, but when her actions become increasingly uncharacteristic she fears her experiment is dangerously out of control.

title: The Informant!
evidence: Mark Whitacre’s bipolar diagnosis is part of his story in this biographical film.
synopsis: A rising star at agri-industry giant Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), Mark Whitacre suddenly turns whistleblower. Even as he exposes his company’s multi-national price-fixing conspiracy to the FBI, Whitacre envisions himself being hailed as a hero of the common man and handed a promotion.

title: The Killing of Kenneth Chamberlain
evidence: Kenneth Chamberlain Sr. is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Based on the true story of the events that led to the death of Kenneth Chamberlain Sr., an elderly African American veteran with bipolar disorder, who was killed during a conflict with police officers who were dispatched to check on him.

title: The Listener
evidence: A caller struggling with bipolar disorder appears briefly in this film’s crisis-line conversations.
synopsis: Beth is a helpline volunteer – part of the small army that gets on the phone every night across America, fielding calls from all kinds of people feeling lonely, broken, hopeless. Over the last year the tide has become a tsunami. As Beth goes through her shift, the stakes rise: is this the night she will lose someone? Save someone? Eventually, Beth’s own story comes to light, revealing why she does it. All along we remain with her: listening, comforting, connecting – patching the world back together, one stitch at a time.

title: The Mess
evidence: Performer Ellice Stevens shares her experience of bipolar disorder in this documentary short.
synopsis: As Ellice gets low, her room gets messy - she never sees it coming, but it always happens. There seems to be no way to break out of the endless highs or lows that make up bipolar, or even to pick up her clothes up off the floor.

title: The Next Great American Game
evidence: Game designer Randall Hoyt discusses bipolar disorder and creativity in this documentary.
synopsis: Randall Hoyt is an aspiring game designer on the road to publishing his first board game. His wry observations about life, gaming and his own struggles with being bipolar drive this story about what it takes to get a board game published.

title: The Not So Secret Life of the Manic Depressive: 10 Years On
evidence: The programme revisits people living with bipolar disorder ten years after Stephen Fry’s earlier documentary.
synopsis: Ten years ago, in an award-winning series, Stephen Fry first spoke about living with manic depression and began a national conversation about mental health. A decade later, we return to the subject to understand where he and thousands of others diagnosed with bipolar (as it is now called) are now.

title: The Only Living Boy in New York
evidence: Thomas describes his mother Judith as depressed and bipolar.
synopsis: When a young man learns that his overbearing father is having an affair, he tries to stop it, only to be seduced by the older woman as well.

title: The Other Half
evidence: Emily lives with rapid-cycling bipolar I disorder.
synopsis: A grief-stricken man and a bipolar woman fall in love and attempt to forge a simple life together.

title: The Outrun
evidence: Rona’s father Andrew lives with bipolar disorder and experiences depressive and manic episodes.
synopsis: Fresh out of rehab, Rona returns to the Orkney Islands—a place both wild and beautiful, right off the Scottish coast. Now 29 and after more than a decade of living life on the edge in London, where she both found and lost love, Rona attempts to come to terms with her troubled past. As she reconnects with the dramatic landscape where she grew up, memories of her traumatic childhood merge with more recent challenging events that have set her on the path to recovery.

title: The Perfect Guy
evidence: Robert Adams is called bipolar in a brief exchange that also describes psychosis.
synopsis: With a fulfilling career and a loving relationship, lobbyist Leah Vaughn seems to have it all. Things come crashing down when Dave, her long-term boyfriend, disagrees with her future plans for marriage and a family. The resulting painful breakup leaves Leah heartbroken, until she meets the charming and handsome Carter Duncan. Soon, the budding romance turns dangerous as Carter reveals his volatile nature, forcing Leah to break up with the man she thought was Mr. Right. She soon realizes that Carter doesn't want to let her go.

title: The Polar Boy
evidence: Hanna lives with bipolar disorder, while Mattias only pretends to share her diagnosis.
synopsis: Mattias has a dream to become a photography student of the Berlin Arts Academy. On the journey of following his calling, his dream is constantly put to a test after Mattias falls in love with a beautiful free spirit Hanna. Trying to win her heart, Mattias feels the need to prove Hanna, that he can be just as adventurous and unpredictable as she is. Breaking the law together with Hanna, Mattias risks everything dear to him, not knowing yet, that Hanna's bold acts are only the symptoms of bipolar disorder. In the moment of jelousy Mattias accidentally commits a crime that could put him behind bars for years. The only escape he sees is to get himself declared irresponsible. In order to achieve that Mattias decides to start faking the illness her gilfriend really has - bipolarity.

title: The Queen of Basketball
evidence: Basketball legend Lusia Harris discusses her bipolar diagnosis in this documentary.
synopsis: Part of the Almost Famous series. She was arguably the greatest women's basketball player. She won three national trophies; she played in the ’76 Olympics; she was drafted to the NBA. But have you ever heard of Lucy Harris?

title: The Restless
evidence: Damien lives with bipolar disorder, a central concern in this family drama.
synopsis: Leila and Damien are deeply in love. Despite his bipolar disorder, he tries to pursue his life with her, knowing he may never be able to offer her what she desires.

title: The Road to Ruane
evidence: Billy Ruane’s bipolar disorder is part of this documentary about his life.
synopsis: Billy Ruane, storied impresario of the 90s Boston indie music scene. Billy promoted shows and inspired cult-like followings of bands by the likes of The Lemonheads, Dinosaur Jr., Pixies, Superchunk, Buffalo Tom, Elliott Smith, Pavement, and Sonic Youth. His gracious treatment of artists set new standards in music. But underneath Billy’s exuberant cartoon-like demeanor and Harvard education, was the pain of a man with deep trauma, who struggled with bipolar disorder and substance abuse, and was confounded by the weight of an endless supply of money.

title: The Salvation Of The World As We Know It
evidence: Paul, the teenage protagonist, lives with bipolar disorder and depression.
synopsis: At first glance, Paul is just a normal eighteen-year-old. What no one knows is that Paul is bipolar. He is helplessly at the mercy of the radical mood swings in his brain. When a depressive episode ends in a suicide attempt, his single father Hardy has to commit him to a therapy center for mentally ill teenagers. At the clinic, Paul meets teenagers who are also struggling with mental problems. He has to make a decision: Does he continue to run away from his illness?

title: The Scream Queen: Daffney
evidence: Wrestler Daffney’s bipolar disorder is part of this documentary episode about her life.

title: The Scribbler
evidence: Cleo introduces herself as bipolar in a brief exchange with Suki.
synopsis: Suki is a young woman confronting her destructive mental illness using "The Siamese Burn," an experimental machine designed to eliminate multiple personalities. The closer Suki comes to being "cured," she's haunted by a thought... what if the last unwanted identity turns out to be her?

title: The Space Between
evidence: Micky Adams's daughter discusses his bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Micky Adams, an eccentric has-been rock musician, loses his grip on reality as his record label looks to drop him and his new "unique" albums. In hopes of breaking out of the mailroom, young Charlie Porter is tasked with traveling to the musician's bizarre home and forcing Micky out of his contract. Micky realizes Charlie could be the key to an artistic breakthrough and the pair's unlikely friendship grows. The odd but powerful bond helps both gain perspective on the music industry, life, love... and the space between.

title: The Ultimate Playlist of Noise
evidence: Alex Lund was diagnosed with bipolar I disorder at 13, a fact his mother discusses in the film.
synopsis: After learning he must undergo brain surgery that will render him deaf, Marcus, an audio-obsessed high school senior, decides to seize control of his fate by recording the Ultimate Playlist of Noise — a bucket list of all his favorite sounds.

title: The Versions of My Mind
evidence: Jimena lives with conditions described as schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Jimena is a patient diagnosed with schizophrenia and bipolar-depressive disorder. Limited by psychiatric treatment, she must sacrifice fulfilling herself as a professional to what she dedicated herself studying, psychoanalysis. Now, she's learning how to live with the existing versions in her mind and is involved in a constant struggle with herself.

title: The Wind at My Door
evidence: Pierre Goupil’s life with bipolar disorder is the focus of this intimate documentary.
synopsis: In this feature documentary, filmmaker Pierre Goupil, suffering from bipolar disorder, recounts his difficult relationship with the disease and looks back on his journey as an artist in a society that does not accept marginalized people. The film celebrates creation, social ties and the freedom of the individual in the face of all the powers that enslave.

title: The Year Between
evidence: Clemence Miller faces a bipolar diagnosis in a story drawn from writer-director Alex Heller’s own experience.
synopsis: Inspired by true events, college sophomore Clemence Miller is coming home to the suburbs and a bedroom in her family's basement. After dropping out of school with a newly diagnosed mental illness, she now faces the challenges of bipolar disorder, the responsibilities of adulthood, and her damaged relationships with family and friends. Clemence struggles to figure out what it means to heal without driving everyone around her… well, crazy. As if reckoning with everything and everyone she has taken for granted wasn’t enough, Clemence has to wrestle with the thought that on top of it all, she might also just have a really bad personality.

title: This Is My Mother
evidence: Judith Haddad leaves a clinic where she has been receiving treatment for bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Pierre, a successful 33-year-old florist, has his life turned upside down by the sudden arrival of his mother Judith, whom he hasn’t seen for two years. Mercurial and extravagant, she suffers from bipolar disorder and has recently escaped from a clinic. Pierre has only one idea in mind: bring her back as quickly as possible so his life can get back on track. But nothing happens as he hoped for. Their unexpected reunion, as funny and explosive as it is heart-wrenching, will transform Pierre and Judith forever.

title: Tik Tok
evidence: A doctor attributes a male patient's symptoms to post-traumatic stress and bipolar disorder.
synopsis: When a bombing occurs during a soccer match between China and South Korea, the two countries are embroiled in a fierce cat-and-mouse chase.

title: To the Bone
evidence: Judy, Ellen’s mother, is called bipolar during a discussion of her hospitalisations.
synopsis: A young woman dealing with anorexia meets an unconventional doctor who challenges her to face her condition and embrace life.

title: To Write Love on Her Arms
evidence: Renee Yohe is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder, though this concerns the film character rather than a confirmed real-life diagnosis.
synopsis: The story follows 19-year-old Renee who has always loved fairy tales: the idea of a princess, a hero and a happily ever after. But Renee’s life is that of a darker tale: she’s a young woman battling addiction, depression and self-injury. In a creative blend of artistic fantasy balanced with harsh reality, the movie follows Renee on her courageous journey towards recovery.

title: Touched with Fire
evidence: Poets Carla and Marco both live with bipolar disorder in this film.
synopsis: Two young poets with bipolar disorder begin a highly passionate, volatile relationship that threatens both their futures.

title: Transference: A Bipolar Love Story
evidence: The film centres on a relationship affected by bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Katarina, a Norwegian nurse in London, embarks on a passionate affair with a fellow immigrant nurse that suffers the consequences of unresolved mental health issues from the lovers' secret pasts.

title: Troubled Minds: The Lithium Revolution
evidence: This documentary traces the history of lithium treatment for bipolar disorder.
synopsis: In a disused hospital pantry in the 1940s, an Australian doctor discovered an astonishing treatment for bi-polar disorder (or manic-depression, as it was then known). It would change the way we think about mental illness and mark the beginning of psychopharmacology - using drugs to manage psychiatric conditions.  It would take 20 years of struggle before lithium treatment was finally accepted, but the scientists and psychiatrists who followed Cade's lead persevered. Their work has meant a chance at stability for hundreds of thousands of people around the world, and lithium remains the benchmark for bi-polar treatment today.

title: Trust Me
evidence: Anne Chataigné lives with bipolar disorder in this hybrid documentary about her experience.
synopsis: Animated short documentary following a young woman's diagnosis of bipolar: a journey of self-acceptance to challenge everyday stigma. In "Trust Me", a genre-bending short documentary, a young woman uses humour and compassion to share her moving and deeply personal story of coming to terms with her mental health condition. When she starts exhibiting atypical and extreme behaviour, her loved ones trick her into hospitalisation against her will. She is diagnosed with bipolar disorder which starts her challenging journey of self-acceptance, confronting internalised and societal stigma, and learning to trust herself and others again.

title: Two Lovers
evidence: Leonard’s mother mentions that he still has a bipolar problem.
synopsis: A depressed man moves back in with his parents following a recent heartbreak and finds himself with two women.

title: Two Ways Home
evidence: Kathy learns she has bipolar II disorder and begins treatment.
synopsis: Soul-touching and moving, TWO WAYS HOME compassionately follows Kathy (Tanna Frederick), a woman newly diagnosed with bipolar disorder who is released from prison on good behavior and returns to her country home in Iowa to reconnect with her estranged 12-year-old daughter (Rylie Behr) and her cantankerous elderly grandfather (Tom Bower).  Her return home is turbulent and a rough, unwelcome transition in which Kathy must come to terms with her diagnosis and its implications on her identity, while also realizing that her family was happier when she was gone. Conflict with her family intensifies as she struggles to keep her head above water, putting her self-worth and well-being to the ultimate test.

title: Type 2
evidence: This short explores bipolar II disorder and its effect on a relationship.
synopsis: Type 2 is a short film that dives into how a toxic relationship can exacerbate the symptoms of bipolar type 2 disorder. It can bring a person to the point of no return.

title: Ulbert
evidence: Artist Joe Ulbert’s experience of bipolar disorder is the focus of this film.

title: Up/Down
evidence: People who report bipolar diagnoses share their experiences in this documentary.
synopsis: There are approximately 5.7 million people in the United States with bipolar disorder. In an attempt to eliminate the mystery and misinformation surrounding the illness, many throughout the country diagnosed with this condition were interviewed extensively. They diligently explain the struggle to balance themselves between floating to a state of euphoria and sinking to a devastating depression.

title: Uproot
evidence: Director Queena Liu and her family talk openly about her father’s bipolar disorder for the first time. He was diagnosed in his forties.

title: Vadakkumnadhan
evidence: Bharatha Pisharody has bipolar disorder and conceals his diagnosis from his family.
synopsis: When a young man goes missing for years, his family concludes that he is dead. However, when his mother spots him years later during a pilgrimage, the real reason for his absconding comes to light.

title: Viplas/Rachana
evidence: Painter Rachana lives with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A painter with bipolar disorder realises the true meaning of art when she learns to let go and finds herself at home in a mental health centre.

title: Vivien Leigh, autant en emporte le vent
evidence: Vivien Leigh’s bipolarity is a central subject of this documentary portrait.
synopsis: In "Gone with the Wind" she was an unforgettable Scarlett O'Hara. Beauty, two-time Oscar winner, celebrated Hollywood star and great Shakespearean interpreter - Vivien Leigh was all that. Behind the celebrity, however, was a fragile person. Her bipolar disorder clouded her success and her private happiness.

title: Walking Man
evidence: Mark and Eric Norwine, a father and son, share their experiences of bipolar disorder during their walk across Missouri.
synopsis: After a Missouri high school loses three students to suicide in seven weeks, a father and son walk 200 miles across the state to find an answer to Missouri's rural suicide epidemic. Both men suffer from bipolar disorder, sharing their struggles with strangers and each other for the first time.

title: We Are Skateboarders: A Mental Health Transformation
evidence: Ben Duffy's documentary presents his experience of living with undiagnosed bipolar disorder.
synopsis: This autobiographical experimental documentary explores the story behind Ben Duffy’s first film, We Are Skateboarders, and the 15-year mental health journey that followed. Ben was 19 and living with undiagnosed bipolar disorder when he made the film. Although it became the second most-watched skateboarding documentary after Dogtown and Z-Boys, it was not a commercial success. As attention grew, Ben’s mental health deteriorated, forcing him to question the meaning of success in life and art. His healing began through therapy, where he confronted trauma, shame, guilt, and complex PTSD linked to the filmmaking experience. The documentary captures his transformation from immense pain toward catharsis, self-love, and compassion. It is a raw and inspiring exploration of resilience, creativity, and mental health.

title: We Don't Belong Here
evidence: Max Green is described as bipolar, while a suggestion that Lily might be bipolar remains tentative.
synopsis: A matriarch of a dysfunctional family is pushed to her tipping point by the disappearance of her son.

title: Welcome to Me
evidence: Alice Klieg recounts being diagnosed with bipolar disorder and later rapid-cycling bipolar disorder, before clinicians called her condition borderline personality disorder.
synopsis: A year in the life of Alice Klieg, a woman with Borderline personality disorder who wins the Mega Millions lottery, quits her meds and buys her own talk show.

title: What Happened, Miss Simone?
evidence: Nina Simone's daughter reflects on her mother's moods and bipolar disorder.
synopsis: The film chronicles Nina Simone's journey from child piano prodigy to iconic musician and passionate activist, told in her own words.

title: When delusion becomes reality
evidence: Jöran Moerkens discusses living with bipolar disorder in this personal documentary.
synopsis: Jöran has a bipolar disorder, which makes him vulnerable to depression, mania and psychosis. He can sympathize well at the moment, but that has been different in the past. Jöran delves into his dark past and talks to the people who experienced his illness up close. How do you deal with this disorder and the misunderstood behavior that comes with it? And how do you break the taboo that still exists on disease pressure?

title: Wild Cloudberries
evidence: Hilla lives with bipolar disorder in this short film.
synopsis: Bipolar Hilla cannot help but fall in love when she meets bohemian and free-spirited Jemina.

title: Wir für immer
evidence: Lina lives with bipolar disorder in this story about a mother and her son.
synopsis: Sixteen-year-old Jann shields his mother Lina from the outside world in a system that has been established over the years. When Jann falls in love with Selma, who is a year older than him, he is less and less able to keep his family secret. Selma and Jann's love causes his previous world to collapse, but ultimately it also gives him the strength he needs to claim a new place for himself in life.

title: Xabi: A Phantasmagoric Adventure
evidence: Four people discuss experiences described as bipolar symptoms in this documentary, without assigning a diagnosis to any one participant.
synopsis: 4 people with psycho-social disability share their stories. Guided by an inner child animation, we will follow their struggle and their way in being a functional human being in a society that rejects them. The film will discuss the issue of Schizophrenia, bipolar, major depression and adult ADHD.

title: You Will Meet a Tall Dark Stranger
evidence: Greg Clemente’s off-screen wife is described as bipolar.
synopsis: Two married couples find only trouble and heartache as their complicated lives unfold. After 40 years of marriage, Alfie leaves his wife to pursue what he thinks is happiness with a call girl. His wife, Helena, reeling from abandonment, decides to follow the advice of a psychic. Sally, the daughter of Alfie and Helena, is unhappy in her marriage and develops a crush on her boss, while her husband, Roy, falls for a woman engaged to be married.

title: Yung Lean: In My Head
evidence: Musician Yung Lean’s struggles with bipolar disorder and drug use are part of this documentary.
synopsis: When a Swedish teen rapper finds a rabid fanbase via the internet, international superstar Yung Lean is born. But as his fame grows, darkness settles in, blurring the line between reality and his own vivid imagination.

title: ZAAD
evidence: Dries Meddens explores his father’s bipolar disorder and his own fear of inheriting it.
synopsis: ZAAD tells the autobiographical story of Dries Meddens. After the death of his mother, the care for Dries' bipolar father falls on his plate. He discovers how crudely and ruthlessly society and psychiatry treat patients. His father eventually dies in solitary confinement. While emptying his parent’s home, Dries discovers an old letter from his grandfather. The man appears to have led a busy, productive life. He is the founder of an internationally renowned seed breeding company and still has time to paint, write diaries and conduct intensive correspondence. Dries finds similarities between his grandfather, his father and himself. Slowly the fear grows that his father's psychiatric illness might be hereditary. Strolling through the family’s film and photo archives, with dramatic and sometimes hilarious finds, Dries tries to find answers. He also consults a psychiatrist. Together the consultations and reviewing of his archival material help Dries look at bipolarity with new eyes.

title: Ça tourne dans ma tête
evidence: Director Louiselle Noël speaks about receiving a bipolar diagnosis as an adult while the film also introduces children with the condition.

title: 清醒边缘
evidence: Wu Hao lives with bipolar disorder in this documentary.

title: A Long Way Down
evidence: Jess is described as having bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Four lost souls—a disgraced TV presenter, a foul-mouthed teen, an isolated single mother, and a failed musician—decide to end their lives on the same night, New Year's Eve. When this disillusioned quartet of strangers meet unintentionally at the same suicide hotspot, a London high-rise with the well-earned nickname Topper's Tower, they mutually agree to call off their plans for six weeks, forming an unconventional, dysfunctional family. They become media sensations as the Topper House Four and search together for reasons to keep on living.

title: Abraxas
evidence: Jonen, a former punk rocker turned Buddhist priest, lives with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Former punk rocker Jonen, now a Buddhist priest, seems to have lost the meaning of his life. His manic depression handicaps him further. Music seems to be the only solution for him to exorcise his demons, against all obstacles and sound volume controllers.

title: Americathon
evidence: Monty Rushmore is described as having bipolar disorder in this political satire.
synopsis: In a story told in narrative flashbacks, a young TV consultant is hired by the President of a bankrupt USA to organize a telethon in order to prevent the country from being repossessed by wealthy Native Americans.

title: An Unmarried Woman
evidence: Elaine’s history of bipolar disorder comes up in a conversation about her lithium treatment.
synopsis: A wealthy woman from Manhattan's Upper East Side struggles to deal with her new identity and her sexuality after her husband of 16 years leaves her for a younger woman.

title: And Everything Is Going Fine
evidence: Spalding Gray recounts being told he had bipolar disorder and describes treatment with lithium.
synopsis: From the first time he performed Swimming to Cambodia - the one-man account of his experience of making the 1984 film The Killing Fields - Spalding Gray made the art of the monologue his own. Drawing unstintingly on the most intimate aspects of his own life, his shows were vibrant, hilarious and moving. His death came tragically early, in 2004; this compilation of interview and performance footage nails his idiosyncratic and irreplaceable brilliance.

title: Ankahee
evidence: Kavya is portrayed as living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A femme fatale sinks her claws into the life of a married doctor and his family.

title: Back from Madness: The Struggle for Sanity
evidence: Bipolar disorder is one of the conditions represented among the four people in this documentary.
synopsis: In part of the HBO's America Undercover series, this documentary provides an insider's view of mental illness, and the use of psychotropic drugs to alleviate some of its symptoms. Tracks the odyssey of four psychiatric patients, beginning with their arrival at Massachusetts General Hospital and the affiliated Lindemann Center, revealing their personal struggles and inner strength as they enter the world of psychiatric treatment to seek relief from insanity.

title: Be Here to Love Me
evidence: Townes Van Zandt’s life with bipolar disorder is part of this documentary portrait.
synopsis: Chronicles the fascinating and often turbulent life of Townes Van Zandt.

title: Bigger Than Life
evidence: The film draws on a real case of psychosis following cortisone treatment, linked to bipolar disorder. The diagnosis belongs to the source patient, not a confirmed on-screen character.
synopsis: A friendly, successful suburban teacher and father grows dangerously addicted to cortisone, resulting in his transformation into a household despot.

title: BiPolar
evidence: This satirical short imagines Santa Claus living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: A satire about a manic-depressive Santa Clause who is addicted to Christmas. The film exposes Santa's sordid off-peak existence, when the newly fallen snow turns muddied and sugarplums go rotten.

title: Call Me Anna
evidence: Patty Duke’s bipolar disorder is part of this adaptation of her autobiography.
synopsis: Patty Duke portrays herself in this made-for-tv biopic about her struggles as a child star growing into adulthood.

title: Chris & Don: A Love Story
evidence: Don Bachardy’s older brother Ted is remembered as having bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Chris & Don chronicles the lifelong relationship between author Christopher Isherwood and his much younger lover, artist Don Bachardy, and it combines present-day interviews, archival footage shot by the couple from the 1950s, excerpts from Isherwood's diaries, and playful animations to recount their romance.

title: Close Calls
evidence: Morgan's grandfather is described as living with bipolar disorder and alcoholism in a brief family conversation.
synopsis: Morgan, a troubled, drug-addled teen, must deal with her crazy grandma and a psycho caller when her father leaves her home alone. As the calls keep coming in, a paranoid Morgan is forced to face some of her worst fears and inner demons when she believes everyone she knows is either plotting against her - or trying to kill her.

title: CM Time
evidence: Hip-hop star Leonardo Hatta lives with bipolar disorder in this film.
synopsis: An advertising agency receives a request from one of their clients, a beverage company. The advertising agency proposes a CM involving the queen of enka who has a difficult personality, an actor  on the downside of his career and a hip hop star. who suffers from manic depression. While filming their CM, the shooting set is thrown into chaos.

title: Crazy Love
evidence: Clayton is portrayed as suicidal and as having bipolar disorder.
synopsis: During his voluntary stay at an Irish mental hospital, manic-depressive Clayton falls head over heels for involuntary schizophrenic patient Anna.

title: D-Tox
evidence: Gilbert is briefly described as having bipolar disorder in the film’s ensemble story.
synopsis: A disgraced FBI agent with a drinking problem joins nine other troubled law enforcement officers at an isolated detox clinic in the wilds of Wyoming. But the therapeutic sanctuary becomes a nightmarish hellhole when a major snowstorm cuts off the clinic from the outside world and enables a killer on the inside to get busy.

title: Derailroaded
evidence: Musician Larry “Wild Man” Fischer’s bipolar disorder is central to this documentary.
synopsis: A documentary on the life and music of manic-depressive, paranoid-schizophrenic cult music icon Wild Man Fischer.

title: Devil's Knot
evidence: Damien Echols says he was diagnosed with bipolar disorder while discussing his psychiatric treatment.
synopsis: The savage murders of three young children sparks a controversial trial of three teenagers accused of killing the kids as part of a satanic ritual.

title: Dialogues with Madwomen
evidence: Seven women discuss experiences that include bipolar disorder in this documentary.
synopsis: A documentary about bipolar disorder.

title: Diploma of Madness
evidence: The story of Ayşe Nil Tahralı’s life is dramatised through Nur, a woman living with bipolar disorder.
synopsis: Nur is a woman who suffers from bipolar depression with psychosis. While she stays in a mental institution she confronts with her life; her childhood, her parents and her marriage...Can she ever learn to love herself?

title: Double Indemnity
evidence: Walter Neff mentions bipolar disorder in the family of a woman he nearly married.
synopsis: An insurance representative is seduced by a dissatisfied housewife into a scheme of insurance fraud and murder that arouses the suspicion of his colleague, a claims investigator.

title: End of the Road
evidence: Sally Clark is described as experiencing severe depression associated with bipolar disorder during a staged therapeutic exercise.
synopsis: Moments after receiving his graduate diploma, Jacob waits at a train station. The future lies ahead, but life abruptly intervenes.
